mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -64.1 to -58.0 over the last four weeks, a steady ~2pt/week recovery trend driven by gradual resumption of shopping and leisure activity. This momentum is expected to continue linearly, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from -64.1 to -58.0
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the linear recovery trend has stalled or reversed.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility decline has been decelerating each week (-1.6, -1.4, -0.4 pts of change). If the week-on-week magnitude of RESIDENTIAL decline falls below 0.5 points, it signals that households have reached a new behavioral equilibrium of time-at-home, which caps further gains in out-of-home retail activity and stalls RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL week-on-week change magnitude falls below 0.5 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL weekly change decelerated from -1.6 to -0.4 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise by more than 1 point per week in the two weeks following a RESIDENTIAL deceleration below the 0.5-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES (-46.0 to -41.4) and TRANSIT (-58.7 to -55.3) have both been improving concurrently. Their joint recovery indicates restored commuting patterns that interact multiplicatively with retail foot traffic near transit hubs and workplaces, producing a stronger positive effect on RETAIL_REC than either series alone over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved every week in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks despite continued concurrent improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous improvement across GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES suggests an active policy regime of relaxed social-distancing restrictions in Hong Kong. Under this relaxation regime, RETAIL_REC is expected to keep rising over the next four weeks as consumer-facing venues continue to reopen and operate with fewer capacity limits.
evidence_refs: fact:all four non-residential categories improved every week in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, and WORKPLACES continue to improve, indicating the relaxation regime assumption is invalid or has reversed.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has risen steadily from -86.6 to -82.6, consistent with summer-season outdoor activity in Hong Kong. Increased willingness to leave home for parks is expected to spill over into nearby retail and dining visits, nudging RETAIL_REC upward over the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -86.6 to -82.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following continued PARKS improvement, indicating no seasonal spillover effect.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has been approaching -55 and is projected to cross above -50 within the horizon. Once TRANSIT exceeds the -50 threshold, reduced friction in commuting and travel is expected to trigger a short-term surge in RETAIL_REC within one week as more people become willing to travel to shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -50 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -58.7 to -55.3 over four weeks, approaching -50
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no uptick in the week after TRANSIT crosses above -50, or TRANSIT never reaches that threshold within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM (-25.3) has recovered much closer to baseline than RETAIL_REC (-58.0), creating a wide convergence gap. As essential shopping normalizes, consumers are hypothesized to extend trips into adjacent discretionary retail and recreation venues, so the GROCERY_PHARM-RETAIL_REC gap narrowing interaction drives RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC is roughly 33 points at t-0w
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC widens or stays constant over the next four weeks instead of narrowing, with RETAIL_REC failing to rise.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week improvement rate across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES has been shrinking (e.g., RETAIL_REC gains of 1.5, 2.6, 2.0 points), suggesting the reopening-driven recovery is decelerating toward a plateau. In a maturing steady-state regime, this deceleration implies RETAIL_REC growth will flatten or reverse over the next four weeks as the easy recovery gains are exhausted.
candidate_trigger: weekly RETAIL_REC improvement falls below 1.0 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gains were 1.5, 2.6, then 2.0 points, showing decelerating improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to improve by more than 1.5 points per week over the next four weeks despite the observed deceleration pattern, rejecting the plateau mechanism.
